markdown_content: # Easily Change Your Pattern Outline Length in CLO | Feature Deep Dive This document explains how to efficiently change the length of pattern outlines in CLO, including working with multiple pattern outlines, adjusting internal lines, handling directionality issues, and using linked lines for precise edits. --- ## Changing Length of Multiple Pattern Outlines This section covers the updated functionality in CLO that allows users to select and change the length of multiple pattern outlines across different patterns simultaneously, improving workflow efficiency. In CLO, you can now select pattern outlines from different pattern pieces at once and adjust their lengths together. Previously, users were limited to selecting one or two segments within the same pattern. To use this feature: 1. Select multiple pattern outlines across different patterns. 2. Right-click and choose **Change Length**. 3. Enter the desired new length value (e.g., 12.5). 4. Adjust the direction option: - **Start**: Adjusts the start of the pattern outline (commonly used for half-symmetrical patterns). - **End**: Adjusts the end of the pattern outline. - **Both**: Adjusts both ends simultaneously (note that this may not apply correctly to half-symmetrical patterns). 5. Confirm by clicking **OK**. This update allows diverse pattern outlines to be adjusted in unison, streamlining pattern editing. --- ## Linking Internal Lines to Pattern Outlines This section explains how to link internal lines to pattern outlines so they adjust automatically when the pattern outline length changes, simplifying internal line management. Adjusting pattern outline lengths often requires repositioning internal lines manually. To automate this: 1. Use the **Transform Pattern Tool** to select an internal line. 2. Right-click on the internal line and select **Link to Pattern Outline**. 3. Choose the specific pattern outline to link the internal line to. 4. Repeat for other internal lines as needed. Once linked, selecting multiple pattern outlines and changing their length will automatically move the linked internal lines accordingly. This feature greatly reduces manual adjustment efforts and helps maintain pattern integrity during edits. --- ## Handling Directional Issues When Changing Length This section discusses current limitations with directionality of pattern outlines when using the Change Length feature and suggests workarounds. When selecting multiple pattern outlines, the direction arrows indicating the adjustment direction may not always align as intended. For example: - Side seams may have arrows pointing in the "same" or "opposite" directions, which affects how length changes apply. - Currently, CLO does not allow users to manually change the direction of individual pattern outline lines within the Change Length tool. - If the direction is incorrect, use this workflow: 1. Select the pattern outline. 2. Right-click and select **Change Length**. 3. Manually choose the direction (Start, End) and input the desired length. 4. Confirm with **OK**. If multiple lines need to be matched precisely after this, use the **Match to Measurement** feature: - Select both lines. - Right-click and choose **Match Up** > **Match to Measurement**. - Choose to match to the longest or shortest line as needed. This enables precise alignment despite directional limitations. --- ## Additional Features for Editing Linked Lines This section outlines other CLO features that enhance editing flexibility with linked pattern lines. - You can right-click and **Link Lines Together** to edit them simultaneously. - Adjustments made to linked lines will affect all linked lines. - You can **Unlink Lines** at any time to edit them independently. - The **Change Length** feature complements these linking options by offering a quick way to adjust multiple outlines. Together, these tools provide a comprehensive set of options to manage pattern outline and internal line adjustments in CLO efficiently. --- # Summary CLO's updated Change Length feature allows simultaneous editing of multiple pattern outlines across patterns, with direction control options. Linking internal lines to outlines automates internal adjustments during length changes. Although direction adjustment per line is limited, workarounds such as manual direction selection and the Match to Measurement tool enable precise control. Additional linking and unlinking features provide flexible editing workflows for pattern designers.
